content: Meperidine, also known by its street names such as Demmies, Mapergan, or Pethidine, is a medication prescribed to alleviate moderate to severe pain. It belongs to a class of drugs called narcotic analgesics, which are similar to morphine in their mechanism of action. Meperidine works by altering the way the body perceives pain. This medication is available in tablet form or as a liquid syrup, both of which are taken orally. It is typically administered every 3 to 4 hours as needed for pain relief, with or without food. Patients must follow the exact instructions provided on their prescription label and consult their healthcare provider or pharmacist if they have any questions. The tablets should be swallowed whole and must not be split, chewed, or crushed, as doing so can lead to misuse or abuse, which may result in severe side effects or even death. For the syrup form, the prescribed dose should be mixed with half a glass of water before consumption to avoid numbing of the mouth. The dosage of meperidine may be adjusted by the prescribing physician based on the patient’s response to treatment and any side effects experienced. Patients should communicate openly with their doctor about their pain levels and any adverse effects. It is important to note that meperidine has the potential to be habit-forming. Patients must not take larger doses, use it more frequently, or continue its use for longer than directed by their doctor. If the medication has been used for an extended period, it should not be discontinued abruptly without medical guidance, as this can lead to withdrawal symptoms. These symptoms may include restlessness, watery eyes, nasal congestion, yawning, sweating, chills, muscle pain, irritability, nervousness, stomach pain, nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, diarrhea, rapid breathing, rapid heartbeat, and back pain. To prevent withdrawal, the doctor will likely taper the dose gradually. Meperidine may also be prescribed for off-label uses. Patients should consult their doctor or pharmacist for further information if this applies to them. Before starting meperidine, patients must inform their doctor or pharmacist if they are allergic to meperidine or any other medications. They should also disclose all prescription and nonprescription drugs, vitamins, supplements, and herbal products they are currently taking. Certain medications, such as antidepressants, sedatives, muscle relaxants, and monoamine oxidase inhibitors (MAOIs), may interact with meperidine, necessitating dose adjustments or close monitoring for side effects. Additionally, patients should inform their doctor if they have a history of substance abuse, heavy alcohol consumption, recent surgery, or any of the following conditions:g., asthma, COPD), sickle cell anemia, pheochromocytoma, spinal abnormalities affecting breathing, enlarged prostate, urethral stricture, arrhythmias, seizures, gastrointestinal issues, or thyroid, liver, kidney, or lung disease. Pregnant or breastfeeding individuals should notify their doctor before using meperidine. If a patient becomes pregnant while taking this medication, they should contact their healthcare provider immediately. Patients undergoing surgery, including dental procedures, must inform their surgeon or dentist that they are taking meperidine. Meperidine can cause drowsiness, so patients should avoid driving or operating heavy machinery until they understand how the medication affects them. Alcohol and recreational drugs should be avoided, as they can exacerbate the side effects of meperidine and lead to serious harm or death. The medication may also cause dizziness, lightheadedness, or fainting, particularly when standing up quickly. To minimize this risk, patients should rise slowly from a lying or seated position. Unless otherwise directed by their doctor, patients can maintain their normal diet while taking meperidine. If a dose is missed and the medication is being taken on a regular schedule, the missed dose should be taken as soon as remembered, unless it is close to the time for the next dose. In such cases, the missed dose should be skipped, and the regular dosing schedule resumed. Double doses should not be taken to compensate for a missed one. Meperidine may cause side effects. Minor side effects include lightheadedness, dizziness, weakness, headache, a sense of extreme calm, mood changes, confusion, agitation, nausea, vomiting, stomach pain or cramps, constipation, dry mouth, flushing, sweating, and changes in vision. Patients should inform their doctor if these symptoms are severe or persistent. Serious side effects, though uncommon, require immediate medical attention. These include slow or difficult breathing, uncontrollable shaking, muscle twitching or stiffness, seizures, hallucinations, irregular or pounding heartbeat, difficulty urinating, fainting, rash, or hives. Any unusual problems experienced while taking meperidine should be reported to a healthcare provider. Serious side effects can also be reported to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program. Meperidine should be stored in its original container, tightly sealed, and kept out of reach of children. It should be stored at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture, and protected from theft. Expired or unused medication should be flushed down the toilet, and patients can consult their pharmacist for proper disposal instructions. In the event of an overdose, contact a poison control center at 1-800-222-1222 or call 911 if the individual has collapsed or is not breathing. Symptoms of overdose may include slowed breathing, extreme drowsiness, coma, limp muscles, cold and clammy skin, slow heartbeat, nausea, blurred vision, dizziness, and fainting. Patients should keep all medical appointments while using meperidine and should not share their medication with others, as this is illegal. Any questions about refilling the prescription should be directed to a pharmacist. Meperidine is marketed under brand names such as Demerol® Hydrochloride and Demerol® Hydrochloride Syrup. Combination products include Mepergan® and Mepergan® Fortis, which contain meperidine hydrochloride and promethazine hydrochloride. Other names for meperidine include Isonipecaine and Pethidine.
